core_obligations: Reduce the assertion for r at least 2 to the case r = 2 by induction, gluing the successive local extensions over the maximal ideals of the intermediate rings into one finite extension with a single local parameter per maximal ideal (chow.tex lines 665-693).

Close the induction on the integer ell = min(length_A(A/a_1A), length_A(A/a_2A)): after replacing A by the finite extension of lines 730-735 in which a_2 lies in (a_1), write a_2 = a_1^m c with m maximal, show m stays maximal after any further admissible finite extension using the boundedness lemma of lines 612-638, and if c is not a unit rerun the same replacement for the pair (a_1, c) so that the length strictly decreases (lines 740-751).
Keep the extension B/A annihilated by a power of the maximal ideal and keep every pi_j a nonzerodivisor at every step (lines 648-653, 659-662).

proof_roadmap.step: Induction on r: apply the r = 2 case to pi_j and a_r inside each local ring B_j, then glue the resulting local extensions with the formal glueing lemma (lines 665-693).

spans.label: reduction to r = 2 by induction and glueing

proof_roadmap.step: Induction on ell: spread a solution from one finite extension A' to A, replace A by the blow-up ring of (a_1, a_2) so that a_2 lies in (a_1), and use the DVR-domination bound to keep m maximal over all admissible extensions (lines 696-739).

spans.label: induction on the minimum length and reduction to the blow-up ring

proof_roadmap.step: Terminate: if the cofactor c is a unit the factorizations are already produced by pi and c; otherwise rerun the replacement for (a_1, c), where the first alternative contradicts maximality of m and the second strictly lowers the length (lines 740-751).

spans.label: termination of the induction on the minimum length

difficulty_reason: The statement asks for one finite extension A contained in B, with B/A killed by a power of the maximal ideal, over which several given nonzerodivisors a_1, ..., a_r simultaneously become unit multiples of a single local parameter at every maximal ideal of B. The proof reduces to r = 2 and then inducts on ell = min(length_A(A/a_1A), length_A(A/a_2A)): local solutions are first spread to A through the formal glueing lemma (chow.tex lines 681-693), A is then replaced by the blow-up ring of (a_1, a_2) built in lines 730-735 so that a_2 lies in (a_1), and the exponent m in a_2 = a_1^m c is shown to stay maximal under every further admissible finite extension by the discrete-valuation domination bound of lines 612-638. What is not routine is the termination step at lines 740-751: the pair must be rerun as (a_1, c), where one alternative is excluded by maximality of m and the other strictly decreases ell, so the induction closes only after combining the glueing, the blow-up and the boundedness input in that order.
